name: Cherry-tomato shakshuka (שקשוקת עגבניות שרי)

source.author: AI-summary screenshot of a TikTok recipe (Hebrew)
source.notes: A quick, fresh shakshuka: a basket of cherry tomatoes blistered in olive oil with garlic and chili until they burst into a sauce, then eggs cracked in, with optional tomato paste. Analyzed strictly as listed, per user request — NO 'upgrade' toppings (goat cheese / bulgarit / feta / basil). Midpoints used: 1 basket cherry tomatoes ≈ 250 g, 5 eggs (of 4–6), 2.5 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tomato paste included, ~½ tsp salt. The source says 4 servings, but at ~680 kcal for the whole pan that's ~170 kcal and ~9 g protein per plate — realistically this is 2 servings (or 1 big one). Stored as 2 servings. A max-protein variant is described in suggested_mods. Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. Estimate.

serving_desc: ½ the pan (~2–3 eggs) — the source's '4 servings' is unrealistically small
steps: Heat the olive oil and cook the cherry tomatoes until they blister and burst into a sauce.
Add the garlic and chili (and tomato paste, if using) and cook briefly; season with salt and pepper.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites are set.

batch_totals.note: WHOLE PAN as listed (5 eggs): ~681 kcal (range ~610 kcal with 4 eggs to ~750 kcal with 6). Fat-led: the 2 tbsp olive oil (~248 kcal) plus egg yolks make up most of the calories; protein is only ~5.2 g per 100 kcal.

him.verdict: Nutritious but not protein-dense as written: the whole pan is ~681 kcal with ~35 g protein (~5.2 g per 100 kcal), because 2 tbsp olive oil is over a third of the calories and the only protein source is the eggs. Good micros — choline and selenium from the eggs, lycopene and vitamin C from the tomatoes (sperm-relevant). The max-protein version (see mods) more than doubles the protein to ~83 g for ~915 kcal (~9.1 g per 100 kcal).
flags: whole pan ~681 kcal / ~35 g protein (~5.2 g per 100 kcal)
very low carb; ~765 mg sodium per half-pan
suggested_mods: MAX-PROTEIN VERSION (whole pan): 6 eggs + 4 egg whites, olive oil cut to 1 tbsp, 150 g cottage 3% dolloped in with the eggs, 100 g bulgarit 5% crumbled on top → ~915 kcal / ~83 g protein / ~28 g carb / ~53 g fat (~9.1 g protein per 100 kcal). Split 2 ways: ~458 kcal / ~42 g protein each
Biggest single lever: cut the oil to 1 tbsp (−~124 kcal) — the tomatoes still blister fine in a nonstick pan
Egg whites are the 'cheapest' protein to add: 4 whites ≈ +14 g protein for only ~68 kcal
Cottage dolloped into the sauce sets into creamy pockets and adds ~16 g protein per 150 g
Serve with a high-protein or whole-grain pita/bread rather than white bread

her_preconception.verdict: A good preconception dish: eggs are a top choline source (fetal brain development) plus selenium and some vitamin D, and tomatoes add vitamin C and lycopene. The one rule in pregnancy: cook the eggs until both whites and yolks are firm — runny shakshuka yolks are a salmonella risk.
prenatal_highlights: selenium, some vitamin D (eggs); vitamin C + lycopene (tomatoes)

safety_advisories.note: Runny/soft yolks carry a salmonella risk in pregnancy — cook until whites and yolks are fully set.
safety_advisories.swap: cover longer until the yolks are firm, or use pasteurized eggs

suggested_mods: Fold in a handful of spinach for folate and iron
If adding the bulgarit/feta 'upgrade', make sure it's pasteurized (it's heated through on top)

cooking_guide: Use a wide pan and medium-high heat so the cherry tomatoes blister and burst rather than stew; press some with a spoon once they soften to release their juices into a sauce.
Add the garlic after the tomatoes have started to burst — added first, it burns before the tomatoes are ready.
If using tomato paste, fry it for 30 seconds in the oil before stirring it through — it deepens colour and flavour.
Make wells in the sauce, crack each egg into a small cup first and slide it in so the yolk stays intact.
Season the whites lightly, lower the heat, and cover; cook until whites are set (and yolks firm for Lihi).
For the max-protein version, pour the egg whites around the whole eggs and dot the cottage in spoonfuls before covering; scatter the bulgarit on top for the last 2 minutes.
